title: The man who built Qwen has a new lab, and the Shanghai government is an investor
excerpt: Junyang Lin, who led Alibaba Qwen, launched Pragmatik Labs in Shanghai. Tencent, HSG, Gaorong and a state fund backed it.
content_html:
The researcher who led Alibaba’s Qwen models has started his own company. Junyang Lin announced Pragmatik Labs on X on Tuesday evening, five months after walking out of Alibaba.

The lab is based in Shanghai and works on what Lin calls next-generation agents across digital and physical worlds. Gaorong Ventures and HSG, the firm formerly known as Sequoia China, co-led the round.

Tencent invested too. So did one more backer, and it is the one nobody else reported.

The investor everyone missed

Lin thanked the Shanghai Engine Fund, giving its Chinese name in the same breath. That name translates as the Shanghai Future Industries Fund.

It is not a private firm. The fund runs to 10 billion yuan, roughly $1.4bn, and is financed entirely by the Shanghai government.

Shanghai unveiled it in September 2024 with a 15-year horizon, extendable by three more. It targets six areas the city has designated as future industries, and it invests both directly and through sub-funds.

None of the major coverage carried this. The Information named Gaorong and HongShan. Bloomberg named Gaorong, HSG and Tencent, and the state money appears only in Lin’s own post.

Why the name is the thesis

Lin did not come to AI through computer science. He holds a bachelor’s degree in English literature and a master’s in linguistics from Peking University, where he later led a group at the Institute of Computational Linguistics.

He joined Alibaba’s DAMO Academy in 2019 and worked on language generation for Taobao search before Qwen. The lab’s name comes from that first act.

“I studied linguistics because my friend recommended pragmatics to me,” he wrote. “The name just means being back to where it happens.”

Pragmatics is the study of meaning in context, which is a reasonable description of what an agent has to do. Lin also invoked pragmaticism, judging a system by how well it works in the world rather than on a benchmark.

What he is actually building

Pragmatik’s own site splits the work four ways. Digital agents for knowledge work, physical agents for real environments, frontier research, and products shaped by real-world feedback.

The physical half is the expensive half. Digital agents need planning, tool use and memory, while physical agents add perception, spatial reasoning and machines that move.

Doing both at once is a much larger bill than building an app on someone else’s model. Lin has not said what the physical agents are, and the term usually points at robots.

China is already the place that builds them. The country ships almost every humanoid robot sold worldwide, so the supply chain sits on Lin’s doorstep.

The exit that started it

Lin left Alibaba on 4 March, posting “Bye my beloved Qwen”. Two other senior figures had gone in the same stretch, and he had warned publicly about the gap between Chinese and American AI.

His Qwen record is the collateral. He was an author on the original 2023 technical report and a core contributor to Qwen2.5, and the family became the base for Alibaba’s AI products.

Alibaba has not stood still. It shipped Qwen 3.8-Max this month, its largest model yet, and let developers customise it.

Lin also championed open weights, an approach that looked shaky at Alibaba around the time he left. The company has since moved back towards it, and it is separately trying to charge its heaviest open-model users.

A wave, not a one-off

Lin is one of many. Elite researchers are walking out of large labs everywhere, and China now has its own crop of what investors are calling neolabs.

The money has followed fast. Chinese AI startups have seen a funding surge that has minted unicorns at speed.

The strategic backdrop is open weights. Cheap Chinese models have created what one analysis called a death zone for American rivals trying to sell access.

Agents are the next front. Alibaba itself has been redirecting models towards agents and robots, which is the same bet Lin has left to make independently.

What is missing

There is no model, no product and no demo. Pragmatik has a website, a mission statement and an email address asking for serious notes.

Lin did not give a valuation. The Information reported in May that he was seeking several hundred million dollars at $2bn, and neither he nor his backers have confirmed a figure since.

Gaorong confirmed the funding and said nothing further. HSG and Tencent did not respond to Bloomberg, and Lin did not respond to a request for comment.

So the round prices a reputation. It buys the Qwen name, the people Lin can recruit, and a research agenda that spans software and machines, before any of it has produced a single released model. The first technical output is the only thing that will settle whether that was cheap or expensive.

为什么这个名字是论文

林并不是通过计算机科学进入人工智能领域的。 他拥有北京大学英语文学学士学位和语言学硕士学位，后来在北京大学计算语言学研究所领导了一个研究小组。

他于 2019 年加入阿里巴巴达摩院，在 Qwen 之前从事淘宝搜索的语言生成工作。 实验室的名字来源于第一幕。

“我学习语言学是因为我的朋友向我推荐了语用学，”他写道。 “这个名字只是意味着回到事情发生的地方。”

语用学是对上下文中意义的研究，它是对主体必须做什么的合理描述。 林还引用了实用主义，根据一个体系在世界上的运作情况来判断它，而不是根据一个基准。

他实际上正在建造什么

Pragmatik 自己的网站将工作分为四种方式。 用于知识工作的数字代理、用于真实环境的物理代理、前沿研究以及由现实世界反馈塑造的产品。

物理的一半是昂贵的一半。 数字代理需要规划、工具使用和记忆，而物理代理则增加感知、空间推理和移动机器。

同时执行这两件事比在别人的模型上构建应用程序的费用要大得多。 林并没有说物理代理是什么，这个词通常指的是机器人。

中国已经是建造它们的地方了。 全世界售出的几乎所有人形机器人都由中国运送，因此供应链就在林的家门口。

启动它的出口

3月4日，林书豪离开阿里巴巴，并发布“再见我心爱的Qwen”。 另外两名资深人士也曾经历过同样的事情，他曾公开警告过中美人工智能之间的差距。

他的 Qwen 唱片就是抵押品。 他是2023年原始技术报告的作者和Qwen2.5的核心贡献者，这个家族成为阿里巴巴人工智能产品的基地。

阿里巴巴并没有坐以待毙。 该公司本月发布了迄今为止最大的型号 Qwen 3.8-Max，并允许开发人员对其进行定制。

林书豪还支持开放式举重，但在他离开阿里巴巴时，这种做法看起来并不稳固。 此后，该公司又重新采取了这一做法，并单独尝试向其最重的开放模型用户收费。

一波，不是一次性

林是众多人之一。 精英研究人员正在走出世界各地的大型实验室，而中国现在也拥有了自己的一批被投资者称为“新实验室”的产品。

钱也跟着来得快。 中国人工智能初创公司的资金激增，独角兽迅速诞生。

战略背景是开放权重。 廉价的中国模式为试图出售准入机会的美国竞争对手创造了一个分析所称的“死亡区”。

代理商是下一个战线。 阿里巴巴本身一直在将模型转向代理和机器人，这也是林自己独立做出的赌注。

缺什么

没有模型，没有产品，也没有演示。 Pragmatik 有一个网站、一份使命宣言和一个要求认真笔记的电子邮件地址。

林没有给出估价。 《The Information》5 月份报道称，他正在寻求 20 亿美元的数亿美元融资，但此后他和他的支持者都没有证实这一数字。

高榕确认了这笔资金，但没有再多说什么。 HSG 和腾讯没有对彭博社做出回应，林也没有回应置评请求。

所以圆形价格享有盛誉。 在生产出单一发布的模型之前，它购买了 Qwen 的名字、Lin 可以招募的人员以及涵盖软件和机器的研究议程。 第一个技术输出是唯一能决定它是便宜还是昂贵的东西。
